solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Aged reporters faffing over Times leader, which is degenerative

definitions.note: a phrase describing a thing, standing in for a noun phrase

indicators.note: faffing is dithering about aimlessly, so the letters are messed around into a new order
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Times is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the opening letter of Times

explanation.surface: A dig at elderly hacks fussing over the editor of The Times, whose influence is said to be in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of the first two words plus the T are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrograde step is a move backwards, a change that makes things worse, which is what something degenerative brings.

clue.text: In favour, China – kid on the block?

indicators.note: In tells the solver the answer sits inside the following run of words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of favour and the start of China

explanation.surface: A question about whether a child on the street is pro-China.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like politics but the six letters are lying in plain view across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy street child, a youngster hanging around the neighbourhood.

clue.text: Commons ultimately wants vegetable as Speaker

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: the final letter of Commons
tater is informal for a potato

explanation.surface: The House of Commons wants a vegetable to be its Speaker, a jibe at a dim parliamentary chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Speaker looks like the Commons official; here it is simply someone who speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: One who states something, declaring it aloud, is a speaker; the agent noun formed from the verb to state.

clue.text: Lawless Jeffrey, without hesitation, gets into 'Cain' disguise

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is taken away from the name
getting into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
a disguise changes how something looks, so the name Cain is rearranged

blocks.note: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and peer jailed for perjury
er is the sound of hesitation
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, who served prison time, dresses up as the Bible's first murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is the novelist and Tory peer jailed for perjury; Cain is the Bible's first murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes a state with no order or rule, so it is a synonym for lawless.

clue.text: (& 14dn.) Leak article about end of Nige (no other!) – switch your full attention to this

definitions.text: switch your full attention to this
definitions.note: an instruction, matching the imperative phrase

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the tail of Nige is kept

blocks.note: a drop is a small leak of liquid, or a leak of information
the last letter of Nige
very in the sense of the very one, that one and no other
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: A leaked piece about Nigel Farage demands that readers stop and look at nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Nige is Nigel Farage. The pieces run DROP, E, VERY, THING.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop everything is to abandon whatever you are doing so you can give something your undivided focus.

clue.text: Holes requiring prominent organ and balls obstructions

blocks.note: the eye is a prominent organ of the face
in tennis a let is a serve obstructed by the net and replayed; let also means hindrance

explanation.surface: A smutty line about holes that call for a big organ and balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo is a decoy; a let is a tennis ball obstructed by the net, as in without let or hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelets are small reinforced openings in cloth or leather through which laces are threaded.

clue.text: Conjecture from politician, full of gas

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a Tory is a Conservative politician
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Mere guesswork from a windbag politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or idea offered to explain something, a conjecture.

clue.text: Bloody hell, grass has lifted, revealing Winner!

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: God! is an exclamation like bloody hell
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone swearing because the turf has come up shows who has won.
explanation.definitionFit: The top dog is the one who comes out on top, the dominant victor in a contest.

clue.text: Fish mean to encase artist!

indicators.note: encasing something means enclosing it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: stingy means tight-fisted, mean with money
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A miserly fish shuts a painter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat-bodied sea creature with a venomous barbed tail, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Member and ex-PM said "not to be sniffed at"?

definitions.note: a jokey description, as an underarm is best not smelt

indicators.note: said tells the solver to go by how the name is pronounced, not its spelling

blocks.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
William Pitt was a Prime Minister; his name is pronounced like a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister is described as no small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Not to be sniffed at normally means worth having; here it is literal, the body part whose smell you avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: The underarm is notoriously smelly, so it is a place you would rather not put your nose.

clue.text: Nick's position hurts badly

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters of hurts end up in a muddled order

blocks.note: to park is to position a vehicle
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick finds his stance is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison. PARKHURST is a top-security jail on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkhurst is a well-known British prison, so it is an example of a nick in the slang sense of jail.

clue.text: Labour leader's after straying peer – turn away!

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so the letters of peer drift into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Labour is used
after places the Labour piece behind the other one

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A Labour leader pursues a wayward lord, who is told to get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or rebuff, the same as turning someone away.

clue.text: Good, port-soaked Willy?

indicators.note: something soaked has the liquid all around it, so the port surrounds the other letter

blocks.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A cheerful question about a chap called Willy who has been drinking port.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy is British slang for the penis, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The male organ is a euphemism for the penis, which a willy is in British slang.

clue.text: Paper rubbishing an MP: "wife-abandoning wretch!"

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is writing material made from animal skin, and also a stiff paper imitating it.

clue.text: see 5dn.

clue.text: A groom after pussy remains to be found in this?

definitions.text: remains to be found in this
definitions.note: a description of a place, standing in for the noun

indicators.note: after places the groom piece behind the pussy piece

blocks.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat
taken as written
to comb hair or fur is to groom it

explanation.surface: A bridegroom follows a cat and stays to be discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains looks like a verb, stays; it is the noun, dead bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber where bones and corpses lie.

clue.text: Be without our mag? Not quite – here's one of Brenda's maybe!

the magazine is Private Eye, where the clue appeared

explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a servant or footman, so a royal flunkey would be one of the Queen's servants.

clue.text: "Length", repulsive, is sanctioned

clue.text: Broke, screwed up (shafted by uncaring Conservative leaders) creature

the opening letters of uncaring and Conservative

clue.text: Pisspoor Tory git turning one out

out means removed, so one letter leaves the fodder

explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for nasty, shabby or of very low quality, the same as rubbish or dreadful.

clue.text: Balls delivered pitch to oust leader?

to pitch a ball is to throw it

explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow is to remove a ruler or government from power by force.

clue.text: To authorise and make to look like an arse?

definitions.text: make to look like an arse

blocks.note: first meaning: to give formal approval

blocks.clueFragment: make to look like an arse
blocks.note: second, jokey meaning: to turn someone into a rat, a contemptible person

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is invented: the ending -ify means to make into, and a rat is a despicable person.

clue.text: "Mowlam the predator" hairstyle?

clue.text: What fat cats like rotten: to skim profits?

clue.text: Fancy Surrey's outskirts welcoming relief?
